title: A worker container has no keeper, so a sandbox sleep wipes its work unrecoverably
description:
Raised by the operator, who asked whether we struggle with Cloudflare container inactivity timeouts. We do, and it explains a failure Phase 2 recorded as something else.

THE PLATFORM BEHAVIOUR, already documented in cloud/sandbox/README.md and quoting Cloudflare: after sleepAfter the container STOPS and 'a fresh container starts. All previous state is lost and the environment resets to its initial state.' A named sandbox gives routing to the same Durable Object, NOT a warm disk. cloud/factory/src/sandbox.ts sets SANDBOX_SLEEP_AFTER = '20m' deliberately rather than keepAlive, because a container that never sleeps must be destroyed by something and that something is the Workflow instance which may itself have died. So THE SUPERVISOR'S POLLING IS THE KEEPALIVE.

THE GAP. The ORCHESTRATOR container runs a run keeper that pushes its branch every 60s (TICKS_KEEPER_INTERVAL, cloud/sandbox/entrypoint.sh) — that is what makes a dead orchestrator leave its work on origin. The WORKER container has NO keeper: 'grep -nE keeper cloud/sandbox/worker.sh' returns nothing. A worker holds everything in its filesystem and pushes once, at the end.

So if the sandbox sleeps before the worker finishes, the filesystem is gone and the work is UNRECOVERABLE — no branch, no report, no salvage, because tick 5fg's salvage and tick 7zk's grace window both run at the end, inside the container. Both protect against the HARNESS being killed and against a budget trip. Neither protects against the platform stopping the container out from under them.

WHAT IT EXPLAINS. Run run_9e40b9563bfb493cac1fe6625356e538: the supervisor died at ~13:32 (the 10-minute step cap, tick 2xm), nothing addressed those sandboxes afterwards, the workers went on making model calls until 14:02 — about 20 minutes later — and then produced NOTHING AT ALL. Not a branch, not a report, not even the container-written fallback. I recorded that on tick 5bv as 'orphaned, nobody collected them'. Sleep-and-wipe fits the evidence better, and explains the absence of the fallback report specifically, which an orphaned-but-alive container would still have written.

THE RULE THIS BREAKS is already in .tick/learnings.md, applied to the orchestrator and never to the worker: 'Durability that depends on an agent remembering to push is not durability — push mechanically on a timer.'

LIVE RISK TODAY is mitigated by accident, not by design: post-2xm the supervisor survives and its wave legs address each sandbox roughly every 7 minutes (WAVE_LEG_MS) against the 20-minute window. A healthy run is fine. But the margin is 2.8x, it is nowhere written down as a dependency, and any future change to leg pacing silently eats it — and if a supervisor dies again, every worker's in-flight work vanishes rather than being merely stranded.

WORK:
1. Give the worker a keeper on the orchestrator's model: push the tick branch on a timer so partial work survives a stop it never sees coming. Reuse entrypoint.sh's keeper rather than writing a second one.
2. Write the pacing dependency down where a future change will trip over it: leg/poll interval must stay well under SANDBOX_SLEEP_AFTER, and a test or constant should pin the relationship rather than leaving it to arithmetic in two files.
3. Consider whether a slept-and-wiped worker is DISTINGUISHABLE from other silences. Right now it looks identical to 'never dispatched', which is the collapse-distinct-failure-classes rule again.
notes:
2026-08-25 14:19 - The operator found this by asking a question I had not asked: 'isn't container inactivity timeout a known limitation of CF containers?' Everything needed to spot it was already in the repo — README.md quotes Cloudflare's own 'all previous state is lost', sandbox.ts explains why sleepAfter rather than keepAlive, and learnings.md carries 'push mechanically on a timer'. Three documents, one conclusion, and nobody joined them until asked.
2026-08-25 14:19 - Runs in the first wave alongside 5qj: it protects the work of every worker that follows, including this epic's own.
acceptance_criteria: A worker container's in-progress commits survive the sandbox being stopped mid-work — proven by stopping one and finding the work on origin. The leg/poll-to-sleepAfter relationship is pinned by a constant or test rather than by arithmetic in two files.
